repos.notes: Authors' official repo (footnote on p.1). Implemented in C++ via TAPA (a task-parallel HLS framework); scanner classifies it tapa_only (34 TAPA files, ~1092 HLS pragmas, Vitis HLS 2021.2 per paper). No other subject repos: TAPA is a build-tool dependency; Allo/DFX are only compared baselines.

summary: Found the authors' own repo OswaldHe/InTAR, linked directly in a footnote on page 1 of the paper (https://github.com/OswaldHe/InTAR). Confirmed by README title + Zenodo DOI + arXiv, git-log authors matching Zifan He (Oswald(Zifan) He) and Yingqi Cao (Richard Cao), and GitHub description naming the FCCM 2025 paper. The design is HLS-based via TAPA (Vitis HLS 2021.2), so the repo is an HLS design repo. No other subject repos in the paper; very high confidence.
